ARTICLE 2 : CONTEXTE Cette prestation vise à faciliter les envois de courriers en recommandé, activité manuelle chronophage sans valeur ajoutée, au regard des volumes importants concernés, ainsi que le suivi des accusés de réception, permettant aux équipes utilisatrices de se concentrer sur leur cœur de métier. À titre d’information, il est précisé que les envois proviendront de différents services au sein de l’Organisme. Le nombre d’utilisateurs réguliers quotidien sera variable selon les organismes, et pourra évoluer tout au long de l’exécution du marché, à la hausse comme à la baisse : environ 20 utilisateurs pour la CAF 93. Si pour assurer la continuité de service, la solution implique de la maintenance préventive, les opérations seront planifiées afin de ne pas gêner l’activité et les utilisateurs seront avisés 48 heures avant. Le cas échéant, la maintenance intègrera sans surcoût, les évolutions mineures de l’outil, sous réserve de l’acceptation des organismes utilisateurs. Une solution d’assistance en cas d’évolutions des besoins des Caf : Les évolutions pourront porter sur un changement de personnel en charge du traitement et un changement de nature et de typologie des courriers. En cas de changement des personnes en charge du traitement des courriers, il est demandé que les modifications d’habilitations soient à la main de l’administrateur de la Caf (pour garantir la réactivité). EBVPD – Europos bendrasis viešųjų pirkimų dokumentas, aktuali deklaracija, pakeičianti kompetentingų institucijų išduodamus dokumentus ir preliminariai patvirtinanti, kad tiekėjas ir ūkio subjektai, kurių pajėgumais jis remiasi pagal VPĮ 49 straipsnį (VPĮ 88 straipsnio 5 dalies nuostatų taikymo atvejais ir subtiekėjai), atitinka pirkimo dokumentuose pagal VPĮ 46, 47, 48 straipsnius nustatytus reikalavimus ir, jeigu taikytina, 54 straipsnyje nustatytus reikalavimus dėl kokybės vadybos sistemos ir (arba) aplinkos apsaugos vadybos sistemos standartų laikymosi, kurio forma prieinama interneto svetainėje http://ebvpd.eviesiejipirkimai.lt/espd-web/. Įgaliotoji organizacija – pirkimams organizuoti, pirkimo procedūroms iki sutarties ar preliminariosios sutarties sudarymo atlikti, taip pat atlikto pirkimo procedūrų ataskaitai ar skelbimui apie sudarytą sutartį ar preliminariąją sutartį pateikti perkančiosios organizacijos įgaliota organizacija, nurodyta specialiosiose pirkimo sąlygose. Komisija – viešojo pirkimo komisija. Perkančioji organizacija – specialiosiose pirkimo sąlygose nurodyta perkančioji organizacija. Pirkimas – perkančiosios organizacijos atliekamas viešasis pirkimas. Preliminarioji sutartis – preliminarioji viešojo pirkimo-pardavimo sutartis (jei taikoma), vienos ar k

PĮ 49 straipsnį (jeigu perkančioji organizacija nustato tiekėjo kvalifikacijos reikalavimus); pasiūlymo teikimo metu žinomi subtiekėjai (jeigu perkančioji organizacija nustato reikalavimus dėl subtiekėjų pašalinimo pagrindų). fiziniai asmenys, kuriuos tiekėjas ketina įdarbinti Pirkimo laimėjimo atveju ir kurių pajėgumais tiekėjas remiasi pagal VPĮ 49 (kvazisubtiekėjai) (jeigu perkančioji organizacija nustato reikalavimus dėl fizinių asmenų, kurių kvalifikacija tiekėjas remiasi ir kuriuos, pirkimo laimėjimo atveju, tiekėjas ketina įdarbinti, pašalinimo pagrindų). EBVPD pildomas jį įkėlus interneto svetainėje http://ebvpd.eviesiejipirkimai.lt/espd-web/. Tiekėjas, pildydamas EBVPD, laukelyje „Procedūros tipas“ turi pasirinkti „Atvira“. Teikdamas pasiūlymą CVP IS priemonėmis šį EBVPD tiekėjas turi pridėti kartu su kitais pasiūlymo dokumentais (pasiūlymo pateikimo skiltyje „Prisegti dokumentus“). EBVPD nurodytą informaciją pagrindžiantys dokumentai kartu su pasiūlymu neteikiami. Perkančioji organizacija bet kuriuo pirkimo procedūros metu gali paprašyti dalyvių pateikti visus ar dalį dokumentų, patvirtinančių jų pašalinimo pagrindų nebuvimą, atitiktį kvalifikacijos reikalavimams ir, jeigu taikytina, kokybės vadybos sistemos ir (arba) aplinkos apsaugos vadybos sistemos standartams, jeig

atsižvelgiama į nacionalinėje duomenų bazėje adresu: https://kt.gov.lt/lt/atviri-duomenys/diskvalifikavimas-is-viesuju-pirkimu skelbiamą informaciją. | Tiekėjas yra įsteigtas arba dalyvauja pirkime vietoj kito asmens, siekiant išvengti VPĮ 46 straipsnio 4 dalyje nurodytų pašalinimo pagrindų taikymo. | VPĮ 46 straipsnio 7 dalis EBVPD III dalies D3 punktas | Iš Lietuvoje įsteigtų subjektų įrodančių dokumentų nereikalaujama, užtenka pateikto EBVPD. ===== FILE: files/21108_10206557_unpacked/1_Pirkimo dokumentai_unpacked/SS_priedas_Nr.7_EBVPD_unpacked/README.txt ===== Tai – trumpas EBVPD rinkmenų, kurias rasite šiame ZIP aplanke, aprašymas. espd.XML: XML rinkmena – tai mūsų EBVPD paslaugoms arba kitoms su EBVPD suderinamoms paslaugoms suprantama rinkmena. REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

REPUBLIC OF TAJIKISTAN

TAJIKISTAN DIGITAL FOUNDATIONS PROJECT

Date: November 9, 2026

Assignment Title: Consultancy Service for Advanced Digital Skills Trainings for 1,000 individuals

Reference No.: PIC-TDFP-CS-3

State Institution "Projects Implementation Center for Tajikistan Digital Foundations" of the Executive Office of the President of the Republic of Tajikistan is implementing Tajikistan Digital Foundation Project (thereafter referred to as Project) co-financed by the World Bank and the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC). The total cost of the project is US$46.2 million, of which the IDA grant is $30M, SDC Trust fund is $14.8M and GoTJ share is $1.4M. and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include the Advanced Digital Skills Trainings for 1,000 individuals

 

The consultant will have to perform the following tasks:

Tasks

s, inclusivity considerations, infrastructure constraints, and applicability of skills.

Section I: Program Overview & Background 1.1 Purpose The Department of the Air Force (DAF), Business and Enterprise Systems (BES) Directorate, AFLCMC/GBGD, is issuing this Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) to identify and acquire an innovative, commercially available Digital Adoption Platform (DAP). This platform will replace the legacy Oracle User Productivity Kit (UPK), which is reaching its official end-of-life. User Productivity Kit (UPK), which is reaching its official end-of-life. The primary goal of this acquisition is to secure a modern, sustainable, enterprise-ready software-guided training and performance-support tool. It must streamline content creation, simplify software adoption, and provide real-time in-application guidance for the DEAMS user base. 1.2 Mission Impact & Capability Gap The current solution (Oracle UPK) represents unsupported software and significant technical debt. Its retirement creates a critical operational gap in how training is conducted across the enterprise. The replacement DAP will modernize training material outputs, provide interactive in-application assistance, and reduce the overall training footprint. This capability is designated as a Criticality (1) — Must Have requirement to support continuous financial and enterprise operations. 1.3 Scope of the Target Environment • User Base: Approximately 26,000+ geographically dispersed personnel across 170+ global locations. • Primary Integration: Stable and proven integration with Oracle e-Business Suite (EBS) (including F orms & OAF pages) and modern web applications. • Target Environments: The DAP must be deployable and tested across both Development (Dev) and Test environments before transitioning to

One of the most concerning developments is the emergence of “nudify” or “nudifier” apps, which can turn ordinary photos or videos into sexualised material within seconds. In the past, altering photos, for example by people with a sexual interest in children, required skill and time. Today, premium options allow users of such apps to tailor audiovisual content to their preferences – including by age, ethnic background and other concerning criteria (ICMEC Australia, 2025). This represents a significant technological advance compared with a time when producing such material was far more complicated. The Australian online safety regulator (eSafety) took action against a UK-based company that offered three popular “nudify” services. According to eSafety, these services were used to create child sexual exploitation material, which constituted a breach of Australian online safety requirements. They may pretend to be younger than they really are, claim to be a different gender, give a false description of their appearance, or send photos of other people while pretending to be them ( catfishing). In some cases, a different scenario may unfold: it may be getting to know an adult who arouses the child’s curiosity and their desire to establish and maintain contact. Such a person is active in areas of the online world where children are present, for example, frequently using chats centred around young people’s interests. They may also search for children who match their individual preferences, for example by browsing their profiles on social media platforms or in online games. 14 The behaviours described here are often referred to by the term grooming. The term “grooming” more accurately reflects the gradual process by which an offender builds a relationship with a child, whereas “seduction” may refer to just one of the methods used https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/grooming [accessed: 30 March 2026]. 39 Some parents or carers are afraid of the internet. This is due both to the constant emergence of new materials in this category and to the fact that content depicting the sexual abuse of children who are now adults continues to be distributed, despite the intensive efforts of many organisations involved in removing it from the virtual space. To give you some point of reference, however, we can cite estimates of how much content in the CSAM category is being uncovered. One of the main sources of information on this subject is the US CyberTipline mentioned earlier. Its data show, among other things, that a single image classified as CSAM was distributed for 19 years and appeared in more than 1.3 million reports! The statistical data published regularly are equally alarming. In 2024, almost 20 million reports were submitted to the helpline concerning the identification, in the resources of local Electronic Service Providers, of materials that may depict the sexual abuse of children (NCMEC, 2025). g such individuals, almost 70% of respondents said that they were constantly worried about being recognised by someone who had seen the materials depicting their sexual abuse. Meanwhile, 30% of respondents reported that they had been identified by such a person (CCCP, 2017). Numerous organisations around the world are involved in removing materials depicting the sexual abuse of children from virtual spaces. Despite the efforts being made, the problem remains current. The online world continues to be a place where content depicting the sexual abuse of children — regardless of their age or gender — is available, and statistics used as a reference point for estimating the scale of the phenomenon can be deeply distressing. That is why education about the risks associated with the internet that contribute to the creation of such materials is of key importance. Older teenagers are probably more likely to admit to such experiences with greater ease and openness, while younger ones may find this difficult. This is precisely why younger children require greater attentiveness and sensitivity from adults. Although sexting as part of exploring one’s own sexuality among peers can sometimes lead to positive experiences, it is important to be aware of the risks associated with it. These include, among other things, the distribution of intimate material after a relationship has ended, for example, as an act of revenge by one of the parties. Particular caution is needed when an adult is involved in sexting. Depending on the circumstances, such behaviour may even constitute a criminal offence. 2.1.2 | Grooming and manipulation The second group of behaviours we want to tell you about are those associated with grooming 14 online. Be aware that a person who wants to sexually harm your child may use various methods and techniques to get closer to them and gain their trust. They may pretend to be younger than they really are, claim to be a different gender, give a false description of their appearance, or send photos of other people while pretending to be them ( catfishing). Women may also act alone – in such cases, creating such content may be linked to relationships with other people, including men, and involvement in wider networks of perpetrators (Salter et al., 2021). This shows that we cannot assume that women are “less dangerous” – it is important to remain vigilant towards all adults who have contact with our children, regardless of gender. At the same time, research findings show that early exposure to such content is relatively common and that it may be accidental or unintentional (Dieseth et al., 2026). In the case of adult online behaviour involving drawing children into sexual activity (e.g. asking for photos or engaging in sexually explicit conversations), research indicates that perpetrators are often people known to the child, and many such situations are an extension of existing social relationships (Finkelhor, Turner and Colburn, 2022). Similar findings emerge from research concerning children who were sexually abused directly (offline), with audiovisual materials from these situations subsequently being uploaded to the internet. In such cases, the perpetrators were most often parents, people known to the child or their family, or people in positions of trust (CCCP, 2017). This is consistent with findings indicating that a significant proportion of CSAM is created in the home environment (Salter et al., 2023). The current legacy analog infrastructure limits scalability, resilience, and interoperability. Under this Call for Solutions, the selected vendor will deliver, integrate, install, and acceptance-test a flexible, open-standard, modular Digital IF solution across up to twenty (20) worldwide satellite communications (SATCOM) teleport sites. Increment 1 will establish a fully operational baseline designed to support subsequent capability upgrades and integrations in future fiscal years. SECTION 2 – REQUIREMENT DESCRIPTION PROBLEM STATEMENT Area of Interest: Modular Digital Intermediate Frequency Solu

quires an open-standard Digital IF architecture. However, before committing to a full-scale global deployment, the DoW must validate the operation, interoperability, security, and performance of these modular commercial solutions in a rigorous representative environment. Technical Objective & Scope The DoW seeks a commercial solution for an Increment 1 Digital IF capability set built on a flexible, open standard (e.g., Digital Intermediate Frequency Interoperability compliant), modular architecture. The selected solution will undergo standard site acceptance testing and operational verification to confirm compliance with contract performance requirements and site compatibility. Upon successful acceptance, this operational configuration will serve as the standardized baseline for deployment and installation across up to twenty (20) worldwide SATCOM teleport sites. Mission Impact Successful validation and deployment of this flexible open-standard Digital IF architecture will directly enhance warfighter lethality and survivability by delivering a highly resilient, agile, and survivable GEO-SATCOM capability which rapidly adapts to contested/congested environments. The Government of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Technical Assistance Facility under the Learning Acceleration in Secondary Education (LAISE) Program and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include undertaking a comprehensive assessment of ICT infrastructure and institutional readiness, the status and readiness of Multimedia Classrooms (MMCs), and teachers’ competencies and readiness to deliver ICT-enabled teaching using ICT facilities and MMCs.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: www.dshe.gov.bd or can be obtained at the address given below. The duration of the assignment will be about 06 (Six) months. The assignment is expected to commence in March 2027.

The Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education now invites eligible firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Expressions of Interest will be assessed based on the follo

Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Expressions of Interest will be assessed based on the following criteria:

  • General Experience of the Firm (core business and years in business).
  • Experience in similar assignments of compatible size, complexity and technical specialty in the required area. Experience in development partner-financed contracts will be considered an advantage.
  • Firm’s in-house staffing resources with relevant expertise (extent of relevant expertise available among the staff who are on the firm’s regular payroll). 
  • Firm’s relevant organizational capabilities for the assignment.

Key Experts will not be evaluated during the assessment of Expressions of Interest.

Intraoperative Neuromonitoring conforms to clinical practice guidelines associated with neurosurgery, orthopedic spine surgery, and pain management intervention under general anesthesia. Intraoperative Monitoring (IOM) assists surgeons in performing complex cases and is proven to increase quality of care and clinical outcomes. IOM provides surgeons with real-time feedback on the impact of surgical interventions on the nervous system. 1.3 Scope: The Contractor shall provide non -personal service(s).
